Gymnochanda ploegi is a tiny, transparent glass-perch species described in 2014. Adults reach only about 2.5–3 cm SL, making it one of the smallest members of its genus.

  • Size: up to 3 cm standard length (rarely 3.5 cm)
  • Temperature: 24–28 °C
  • pH 5.0–6.5
These fish are wild caught. This is one of the most difficult fish to keep. Be sure to have the habitat ready before purchase.
Peat-swamp and forest-stream systems of West Kalimantan (Borneo), Indonesia.
It inhabits soft, acidic blackwater with low mineral content, dense vegetation, and subdued light — typical peat-forest habitat.

Very soft, acidic water typical of peat or blackwater.

  • pH 5.0–6.5
  • GH ≤ 2 dGH
  • KH ≤ 1 dKH
  • TDS 20–90 ppm
  • Temperature 24–28 °C; keep stable and well-oxygenated

Clean, stable conditions are essential — absolutely no salt.
Provide gentle flow, soft lighting, and floating plants for cover.
Carnivorous micro-predator. Eats tiny live foods such as micro-worms, daphnia, newly hatched brine shrimp, and small insects. Once settled, may take finely chopped frozen foods or micro-granules.

Very delicate and intolerant of poor water quality or high mineral content. Keep in peaceful groups (6+ preferred) to reduce stress. Tankmates: only very small, peaceful soft-water species, e.g. Boraras rasboras, tiny tetras, Kuhli loaches, small shrimp, or other calm micro-fish from blackwater habitats. Avoid aggressive or fast fish and livebearers.
Males have elongated dorsal and anal fin rays and often display subtle reddish or yellow hues, while females remain more transparent.
Captive breeding is difficult due to small fry and specialized spawning behavior.
